solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Girl in lead circling till race's conclusion

indicators.note: the symbol for lead goes round the word for till, enclosing it

parts.note: Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
to till soil is to hoe it

indicators.note: the conclusion of race is its final letter

explanation.surface: A girl at the front of a race, going round until it finishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lead' looks like the front position in a race, but it is the metal, Pb. 'till' is the verb for working soil, not 'until'.
explanation.definitionFit: Phoebe is a girl's given name, so a girl can stand for it.

clue.text: Pipe outside grand garden building?

indicators.note: the pipe word sits outside the word for grand, wrapping it

parts.note: a hose is a flexible pipe
a grand and a thou are both slang for a thousand pounds or dollars

explanation.surface: A grand pipe running outside a building in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grand' looks like an adjective for the pipe, but it is slang for a thousand, THOU.
explanation.definitionFit: A glasshouse kept warm for growing plants is a structure found in a garden.

clue.text: English team needing authority, but not a crisis

parts.note: XI, eleven in Roman numerals, is a cricket or football side

indicators.note: says the following letter is to be removed from the authority word

parts.note: an agency is an official body with authority

explanation.surface: An English side needs leadership, though things are not at crisis point.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not a crisis' reads as a reassurance, but 'but not a' removes A from AGENCY and 'crisis' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An exigency is a pressing emergency or urgent need, close in sense to a crisis.

clue.text: Give details of displaced person one took in

parts.note: an expat lives away from their home country
I is the Roman numeral for one
to take food in is to eat it, so ate

explanation.surface: Someone asks for details of a refugee whom a person took in.
explanation.definitionFit: To expatiate is to speak or write at length, going into detail on a subject.

clue.text: Visionary stifling a detainee's threat, in the main

indicators.note: the visionary word smothers the next pieces, holding them inside

parts.note: a seer is a visionary or prophet
a POW (prisoner of war) is a detainee; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A prophet silencing a prisoner who poses a threat on the high seas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the old poetic word for the sea, so the definition is a navy's threat at sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Naval strength is the menace a nation can project across the open sea.

clue.text: Enjoying suffering from stomach acid is so silly

indicators.note: silly means foolish or muddled, signalling that these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone takes a perverse pleasure in the pain of an acid stomach.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who gets pleasure from pain, both given and received, is enjoying suffering.

clue.text: Might copy off entertaining figure

indicators.note: the jumbled letters host the number, holding it inside
off means gone bad or wrong, so the letters of copy are rearranged

parts.note: ten is a figure, a number

explanation.surface: A copied version might be missing an amusing character.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Might' looks like a verb but is the noun meaning power. 'off' scrambles the copy letters into POCY before the number goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Potency is power or strength, which is what the noun might means.

clue.text: Our group are going to bother with a lot of funds

parts.note: we is how a group refers to itself
the contraction 'll stands for will, as in we'll go
a to-do is a fuss or bother

explanation.surface: Our team is going to make a fuss about having plenty of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Being well-to-do means being wealthy, comfortably off with plenty of money.

clue.text: Place for the old theorems to get renewed

indicators.note: renewing something remakes it, so the letters are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Old theorems need updating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the old' looks like it describes the theorems, but it belongs to the definition: elderly people.
explanation.definitionFit: A residential home where elderly people are cared for is a place for the old.

clue.text: Charged about drug experience, having no gear

indicators.note: the word for charged goes around the drug word, surrounding it

parts.note: to charge is to rush, so charged means sped
a trip is a hallucinogenic drug experience

explanation.surface: Someone was arrested over a drug episode with no equipment on them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests a police charge, but it means rushed, SPED.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripped means naked, wearing no clothes, and gear is slang for clothing.

clue.text: One going on record wants pen, mostly drunk

parts.note: a sty is a pen for pigs

indicators.note: most of the drunkard word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: a lush is a habitual drunk

explanation.surface: A writer who goes on the record wants a pen, being mostly drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pen' looks like a writing tool but is a pigsty. 'record' is a vinyl disc.
explanation.definitionFit: A stylus is the needle that runs in the groove of a vinyl disc on a turntable.

clue.text: Male with some guts shows force

parts.note: the omentum is a fold of membrane attached to the stomach and intestines

explanation.surface: A man with a bit of courage shows strength.
explanation.walkthrough: 'guts' suggests courage but is literal anatomy: the omentum is a fold of tissue around the abdominal organs.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum is the impetus or driving power of a moving body, a kind of force.

clue.text: Snippet is small, evidently

parts.note: natch is informal shorthand for naturally, of course

explanation.surface: A short extract is small, obviously.
explanation.definitionFit: A snatch is a brief fragment, as of a song or conversation overheard.

clue.text: Swish clothing provided in catalogue?

indicators.note: the smart word dresses the condition word, wrapping round it

parts.note: swish means smart or stylish, as does classy
provided that means if

explanation.surface: A smart range of clothes is offered in a mail-order brochure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catalogue' looks like a noun but is the verb, to list in order; the question mark flags the shift.
explanation.definitionFit: To catalogue items is to sort them into groups, arranging them by category.

clue.text: Scoffed before pal admits "I'm not sure how country may be run"

indicators.note: the joined pair lets the hesitation in, holding it at their junction
the eating word comes first, ahead of the friend word

parts.note: to scoff is to eat greedily; being fed is the result
an ally is a friend or pal
er is the sound of hesitation or doubt

explanation.surface: A well-fed friend hesitantly admits uncertainty about how the nation should be governed.
explanation.definitionFit: A federal nation is governed as a union of states sharing power with a central government.

clue.text: English penned by historian, one leaving draft

indicators.note: the historian's name encloses the letter, as if writing it in
the numeral departs from the historian's name

parts.note: Livy was a Roman historian
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: An English passage written by a historian, with someone leaving a draft.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draft' looks like a written version but means conscription.
explanation.definitionFit: A levy is the conscription of troops, as is a draft.

clue.text: A lot of meat to moisten with juices in pan

indicators.note: most of the meat word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: lamb is a meat
to baste is to spoon cooking juices over meat

explanation.surface: A big joint of meat, basted with juices in the roasting pan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pan' looks like a cooking vessel but is the verb, to criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To lambaste and to pan both mean to criticise severely, as a reviewer might.

clue.text: Very obese queen's dropped acid

indicators.note: says the queen's letter falls out of the size word

parts.note: enormous means very big
R, for Regina, is a queen; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A grossly overweight queen took LSD.
explanation.walkthrough: 'acid' looks like the drug but means sharp-tongued, spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: Venomous remarks are bitter and spiteful, like acid ones.

clue.text: Perform sport, or cheat thereat?

parts.note: to do something is to perform it
PE, physical education, is school sport

explanation.surface: Take part in a sport, or perhaps cheat while doing it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thereat' points back to sport: an athlete may cheat with drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: To dope is to take banned drugs to enhance performance, a way of cheating in sport.

clue.text: Deplorable state of poor sod — a pity!

indicators.note: poor means bad or shoddy, signalling these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sympathises with an unfortunate soul in a dreadful condition.
explanation.definitionFit: A dystopia is an imagined society where everything is wretched, the opposite of utopia.

clue.text: Slip and cloak worn by rogue female

indicators.note: the cloak goes around the other pieces as a garment is put on

parts.note: a pall is a cloak or mantle
a rat is a scoundrel

explanation.surface: A slip and a cape worn by a roguish woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slip' looks like a petticoat alongside the cloak, but means a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: A pratfall is a fall onto the backside, a comic tumble or slip.

clue.text: Area roughly inside toy container

indicators.note: the pieces go into the toy word

parts.note: a teddy is a toy bear
ca, from Latin circa, means roughly or approximately

explanation.surface: An approximate space inside a toy box.
explanation.definitionFit: A caddy is a small box or tin for keeping loose leaves for brewing.

clue.text: Drawing back, holding long tube

indicators.note: the backward art word holds the longing word inside it
the art word is read backwards

parts.note: drawing is a form of art
to long for something is to ache for it

explanation.surface: Pulling back while gripping a lengthy pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drawing back' reads as withdrawing, but 'back' turns the art word into TRA, which then holds the longing word.
explanation.definitionFit: The trachea, or windpipe, is the tube carrying air to the lungs.

clue.text: Clodhopper Garbo bungled lead in Ninotchka

indicators.note: bungled means messed up, so these letters are scrambled
the lead of the film title is its first letter

explanation.surface: Greta Garbo fluffed her starring role in the 1939 film Ninotchka.
explanation.definitionFit: A brogan is a heavy, coarse ankle-high work boot; clodhopper is slang for such a clumsy shoe.

clue.text: Vex one briefly slowing in speed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: the slowing abbreviation goes into the speed word

parts.note: a rate is a speed
rit. is the short form of ritardando, the musical direction to slow down

explanation.surface: Annoy someone by going slowly in a speed zone.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate someone is to annoy them, as to vex does.

clue.text: Calm man's after some smut

indicators.note: the pronoun follows the smut word

parts.note: smut is a flake of soot
he refers to a man; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A man wants a bit of dirty material to steady himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'smut' suggests indecency, but here it is soot.
explanation.definitionFit: To soothe someone is to quieten and settle them, making them calm.

clue.text: Place on phone record for mix of action and dialogue

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after the preceding pieces

parts.note: tel. is the abbreviation for telephone
an EP is an extended-play record
to lay is to place

explanation.surface: Putting a phone call on record.
explanation.definitionFit: A teleplay is a script for television, combining stage directions and spoken lines.

clue.text: Delighted where financiers are still

parts.note: EC is the postcode of the City of London, the financial district
static means still, not moving

explanation.surface: Bankers stay delighted in the same place.
explanation.walkthrough: EC is the postal district covering the City of London, Britain's financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Being ecstatic means being overjoyed, thrilled beyond measure.

clue.text: End of tyranny in good time in each revolution?

indicators.note: the end of the word is its last letter

parts.note: to arrive in good time is to be early

explanation.surface: Tyranny ends promptly in every uprising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolution' suggests uprising, but means one orbit of the Earth around the Sun.
explanation.definitionFit: One orbit of the Sun takes a year, so happening once per orbit is annual.
